shortcut_name: binary-sum uniqueness reduces the task to exact cover
evidence: The survivor groups rows by coordinates and tracks "mask_x, mask_y, mask_z", accepting only when "mask_x == full_mask and mask_y == full_mask and mask_z == full_mask". This relies on each power-of-two sum having exactly the coordinate set {1, ..., k}.
affordance_in_statement: The resonance is calculated using powers of 2: "The frequency resonance is ∑ 2^{x_i}" (and similarly for y and z), with baseline "B_k = ∑_{j=1}^k 2^j".
removal_suggestion: Replace the power-of-two resonance weights with non-superincreasing weights, such as weight j for coordinate j, while defining the baseline as the sum of weights 1 through k. Then matching the baseline with exactly k selected configurations no longer forces every coordinate to be used exactly once.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses binary uniqueness to turn the three resonance equalities into a 3-dimensional exact-cover problem over x, y, and z masks.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The resonance and baseline are both sums of distinct powers of 2, and exactly k configurations must be selected.

common_affordance: The power-of-two sums uniquely force the selected x-, y-, and z-coordinate multisets to be {1, 2, ..., k}, enabling three full-coordinate masks and exact cover.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its dancing-links exact-cover search has exponential worst-case behavior and timed out.
It enumerates every k-subset of the t configurations, causing combinatorial time explosion and TLE.
It reduces the problem to separate bipartite matchings, which does not enforce that the same selected triples simultaneously satisfy all three coordinate constraints.

recommended_edit: Change the resonance definition from powers of 2 to ordinary coordinate weights: use resonance ∑x_i, ∑y_i, and ∑z_i, with baseline 1 + 2 + ... + k. This preserves the input/output format and examples but removes the binary-uniqueness reduction used by the surviving exact-cover solution.
